text:
Cutter Gauthier came into November as a good young winger and is leaving it as, in one reporter's words, the hottest scorer in the league. He has 18 points in his last ten games, and the coverage has him in the Rocket Richard race beside Leon Draisaitl. Colorado's Scott Wedgewood ended his goal streak with a shutout last week. Sportsnet's Eric Engels wondered aloud whether Gauthier, at $13.5 million a year through 2032, might end up underpaid. Our numbers put him at 46% to score tonight, the highest on either side.

The Ducks around him are not having the same month. They have lost three straight, outscored 15-8, and lost Leo Carlsson to an upper-body injury in Utah on Saturday (he is day-to-day) a game after Beckett Sennecke went on injured reserve with 26 points in 22 games. Ryan Poehling is out too. Mikael Granlund, 16 points in his last ten, is on a 100-point pace that the team's own video calls under the radar. Lukas Dostal is the worry: .838 and 5.4 goals worse than expected over his last five starts, .857 for the season.

Seattle is two points behind Anaheim in the Pacific and has its own problems. The Kraken take 45% of the five-on-five expected goals (expected goals measure the quality of chances), have lost four of five, and coach Lane Lambert called the penalty kill "the elephant in the room" after Saturday's loss in San Jose, per Alison Lukan. Jared McCann is out until about January. The bright spot is Berkly Catton, whose first NHL hat trick, against Vancouver, made Kraken history and who has ten points in ten, though our numbers say bounces have helped. Matty Beniers has goals in three straight. Joey Daccord starts at .872 and 3.9 goals below expected.

Two struggling goalies, a division game, and the hottest shooter around: our numbers lean Anaheim on chances, 3.72 expected goals to 3.23.
headline: Gauthier's tear meets a Kraken team in a hole
